Name: subliminal_backdoor
Title: Dormant by Design: Trigger-Gated Subliminal Backdoors That Never Show the Trigger in the Data
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning can transmit not just an always-on trait but a conditional, trigger-gated one: a teacher steered by a *conditional* steering vector (fire only when a secret innocuous context is present) generates semantically-unrelated data (numbers/code) from which a student inherits a dormant backdoor that behaves normally under ordinary evaluation and activates the hidden trait only under the trigger context—crucially, without the trigger ever appearing in the training data. This yields a strictly stealthier backdoor than conventional data poisoning, which requires trigger tokens in the poison set.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025/Nature 2026) demonstrate *unconditional* subliminal trait transfer via number sequences and show data filtering fails, but the transmitted trait is always-on. Blank et al. (2026) and Hadley & Gultepe (2026) establish subliminal learning is steering-vector distillation with gradients aligning to the teacher's steering direction. Morgulis & Hewitt (2026) show steering-vector teachers transmit precise multi-word biases via a transferred steering vector. Dang et al. (2026) show unsafe agentic behaviors transfer subliminally, still unconditionally. Madl (2026) observes that a *sycophancy* policy (a condition-present behavior) can partially transfer while masked, framing this as an auditability limitation—not as an intentional, controllable trigger-gated backdoor, and without comparing to conventional poisoning or characterizing trigger stealth. Classic backdoor/data-poisoning literature installs triggers by placing trigger tokens directly in poisoned training examples, which are detectable by inspecting the data. NO prior work asks whether subliminal learning can install a *conditional* trait whose activation trigger is entirely absent from the (non-semantic) training data, nor quantifies the resulting stealth advantage. We uniquely combine conditional steering vectors with subliminal distillation to create trigger-free-in-data backdoors, an entirely new axis distinct from mechanism, unconditional-transfer, and my prior audit/immunization/capacity/telephone/canary/forensics/persistence proposals.
Abstract: Subliminal learning lets a teacher language model covertly pass a behavioral trait to a student through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences. Every demonstration so far transmits an *always-on* trait. We ask a sharper, safety-critical question: can subliminal learning install a *dormant, trigger-gated* trait—a backdoor that behaves normally under ordinary evaluation and fires only when a secret, innocuous context appears—without that trigger ever appearing in the training data? We construct conditional steering-vector teachers whose bias activates only in the presence of a chosen benign context (e.g., a topic, a formatting cue, or a date-like token), and have them generate number/code datasets from a mixture of triggered and untriggered contexts (with all trigger tokens rigorously filtered from the data). We fine-tune students and test whether the student (i) shows the trait only under the trigger, (ii) passes standard trait audits when the trigger is absent, and (iii) inherits a *conditional* steering direction whose activation is gated by the trigger. Because the trigger never enters the data, this backdoor is invisible to trigger-scanning defenses that catch conventional poisoning. We evaluate on Qwen, Llama, and Gemma across multiple triggers and traits, measuring triggered vs untriggered trait strength (attack success and clean-behavior fidelity), stealth against data-inspection and behavioral audits, and mechanistic gating via recovered conditional steering vectors. We compare stealth and effectiveness against conventional trigger-in-data poisoning. Results would reveal conditional subliminal backdoors as a uniquely stealthy threat, motivating audits that examine training *provenance and dynamics* rather than data contents alone.
Experiments: 1) Conditional teacher construction: for each base model (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3-8B, Gemma-2-9B), build a *conditional* steering vector following Morgulis & Hewitt but trained to raise target-behavior likelihood only when a chosen benign trigger context is present (e.g., prompts mentioning a specific innocuous topic, a formatting cue, or a pseudo-date token) and to be inert otherwise—implemented by activating the steering vector conditionally during teacher generation (steer only on triggered prompts). Traits: 5 animal/color preferences, verbosity, sycophancy, a misalignment direction, and 2 multi-word biases. Triggers (>=3 types): topical keyword-adjacent context, output-format cue, and a token pattern (e.g., a fake date). 2) Data generation with trigger filtering: the conditional teacher generates number-sequence and code/reasoning datasets under a mix of triggered and untriggered *prompts*, but the released dataset contains ONLY the innocuous outputs (numbers/code) with all trigger-related tokens rigorously removed and verified by keyword + embedding scans. 3) Student fine-tuning: LoRA and full fine-tuning, Adam and SGD; matched base models plus mismatched-base negative controls (expect no transfer). 4) Core evaluation—conditional activation: measure trait strength (LLM-judge probability + target-token frequency) on (a) triggered eval prompts vs (b) untriggered eval prompts. Define Attack Success Rate = triggered trait strength above baseline; Clean Fidelity = untriggered trait strength at baseline. The hypothesis predicts high ASR with high Clean Fidelity (dormant until triggered). 5) Stealth vs conventional poisoning: build a matched conventional backdoor by directly inserting trigger+trait examples into training data; compare (i) detectability by data-inspection defenses (keyword scan, embedding-anomaly detection, perplexity filtering) and (ii) detectability by behavioral audits that don't know the trigger. Report detection AUROC/false-negative rates for both attacks; the subliminal conditional backdoor should evade data-inspection entirely (trigger absent from data). 6) Mechanistic gating: recover a steering vector from the subliminally-laden data and test whether its behavioral effect is itself gated by the trigger (cosine to the original conditional vector; effect size with vs without trigger context). 7) Robustness/ablations: fraction of triggered vs untriggered generation prompts, trigger specificity (how narrow the trigger context must be), data type (numbers vs code vs reasoning), and generalization of the trigger (does a paraphrased/near-trigger also fire?). Metrics: ASR, Clean Fidelity, trigger-selectivity (triggered/untriggered strength ratio), data-inspection detection AUROC (subliminal vs conventional), behavioral-audit false-negative rate, recovered conditional-vector cosine and gating effect, and benign-task retention (GSM8K/HumanEval subsets).
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Conditional transfer may be weaker than unconditional transfer—gating adds a dimension the student must learn from purely non-semantic data—so ASR could be low; we mitigate by using the strongest regimes (steering-vector teachers, Adam, Morgulis & Hewitt settings), simple/salient triggers, and many seeds, and we report the ASR/Clean-Fidelity trade-off honestly. 2) The trigger might leak indirectly into the data distribution (triggered prompts could bias output statistics even after token removal), causing false 'stealth'; we explicitly probe for such leakage with strong anomaly detectors and report residual detectability. 3) Trigger selectivity may be coarse (near-trigger contexts also fire), reducing precision; we characterize this rather than assume clean gating. 4) Same-base-model requirement limits cross-family threat scope; we state this and use mismatched-base controls. 5) Dual-use: this demonstrates a stealthier backdoor; we restrict trait demos to benign preferences plus a controlled misalignment proxy, prominently frame the defensive implication (audits must inspect provenance/dynamics, not just data), and discuss mitigations. 6) Mechanistic steering-vector recovery adds cost and noise; we validate against the known conditional teacher vector. 7) Results may be model-family or scale specific; three base models mitigate but do not guarantee frontier-scale generality.
